title: I finally finished a game
author: DoctorLunatic
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been developing games in Unreal Engine for about 10 years, but I've always struggled to actually finish projects. No matter how small I start, they inevitably become too ambitious.

Recently, I've been experimenting with Claude Opus 5.5 and MCP tools, and it's completely changed my workflow.

My latest project, **5000 Donuts**, is a first-person sorting game where you organize thousands of scattered donuts, complete orders, and purchase upgrades.

I used AI with Blender MCP, Substance Designer, and Illustrator to rapidly build the environment, along with some more complex programming systems like hand pathing and physics-based audio.

It's still taken plenty of debugging, iteration, and manual work, but AI has helped me accomplish things in days that previously would've taken weeks. For the first time, I'm actually close to releasing a game!

**Steam page:** [https://store.steampowered.com/app/3934710/5000\_Donuts/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3934710/5000_Donuts/)

Anyone else using MCP tools for game development? Curious how they've changed your workflow.
